title: Day Count Convention Applied to the Bonus Review Span
content:
The day count convention used to settle relationship bonus on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts follows the fee history of the account: the count of fee entries posted to it in the three calendar months ending on the review date.

**Where 5 or more fee entries posted in that window**, the bonus review span in days is divided by a commercial year of 360 days.

**Where 3 or 4 fee entries posted in that window**, the bonus review span is first restated as whole thirty-day months by multiplying it by 0.9863 and rounding to a whole day, and that restated span is divided by the commercial year of 360 days.

**Where fewer than 3 fee entries posted in that window**, the bonus review span in days is divided by the day count basis of 365.

Take a hypothetical bonus review span of 90 days. In the first band the 90 days are divided by 360. In the second band the span is first restated: 90 multiplied by 0.9863 is 88.767, which rounds to 89 days, and those 89 days are then divided by 360. In the third band the 90 days are divided by 365.

The restatement in the middle band is applied to the span itself before the division, and the rounding there is to a whole day, so a restated span is always a whole number of days. A count of exactly 5 fee entries falls in the first band, a count of exactly 3 in the second, and a count of 2, 1 or 0 in the third.
